access_note: The spreadsheet is obtained through a short download form; the map, dashboards and summary tables are open.
description: The Global Integrated Power Tracker from Global Energy Monitor (GEM), a non-profit research organisation, combines GEM's power trackers into one global data set of power plants across all major generation technologies: coal, oil and gas, solar, wind, hydropower, nuclear, geothermal and bioenergy. On 26 September 2026 the page counted 182,400 power facilities with 22,296 GW of capacity in 200 countries and areas, owned by more than 8,000 owners. Summary tables give capacity by technology and status for regions, BRICS countries, Chinese provinces, US states and Indian states. The latest release was September 2026. Coverage is global. Access is through a free online tracker map, dashboards and summary tables, and the full data set is a spreadsheet downloadable through a short download form on GEM's site, under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: it inherits the thresholds and release dates of the component trackers. Simulation uses are building national generation fleets for power system models, hazard exposure of all generation and transition pathway studies. Related records: data-global-power-plant-database is an older global plant list, and the GEM technology trackers are separate records.
